finding.title: Replace DateTime.now() with fixed timestamps in bookmark_dao_test.dart for full hermeticity
finding.why: 5 occurrences (lines 37, 56, 83, 110, 129) use wall-clock DateTime.now() for insert timestamps. None is asserted against an exact value, so this isn't flaky today, but it violates TQ-6's hermetic-test requirement and is inconsistent with the sibling bookmark_dao_extra_test.dart, which uses fixed DateTime.utc(...) throughout in the same directory.
finding.recommendation: Replace `DateTime.now()` with a fixed `DateTime.utc(...)` constant, matching bookmark_dao_extra_test.dart's convention.

finding.title: Replace inline CurriculumTracksCompanion.insert() boilerplate with the existing seedTrack() helper across DAO tests
finding.why: test/helpers/drift_memory.dart already defines seedTrack() with a docstring stating it 'replaces the old pattern of constructing CurriculumTracksCompanion.insert inline in each test' — yet only 1 of 15 files in this batch that seed a track uses it; the other 34 sites hand-roll the companion. curriculum_tracks' shape has already changed 3 times (W3.22, W3.25, W3.28 per in-file comments removing trackType, renaming isActive/deletedAt to state/stateChangedAt), and each change required manually revisiting every inline call site. Call sites routed through seedTrack() get such fixes for free from one place; the other 34 do not, so the next schema change repeats the same N-site shotgun-surgery risk (a site missed during a mass edit silently keeps stale field values rather than failing loudly).
finding.recommendation: Replace `db.into(db.curriculumTracks).insert(CurriculumTracksCompanion.insert(...))` with `seedTrack(db, profileId: ..., curriculumId: ..., activatedAt: ...)` at all 34 listed sites, following the pattern completion_dao_tier_filter_test.dart already uses correctly. Mechanical, no behavior change expected.
acceptance_criteria: All 34 listed call sites replaced with seedTrack(...); test suite still green
No remaining `CurriculumTracksCompanion.insert(` under test/core/database/daos/**, except inside test/helpers/drift_memory.dart itself
Optional Rule-0 checker: add a warn-only grep to make audit for `CurriculumTracksCompanion.insert(` under test/core/database/daos/**/*.dart excluding drift_memory.dart

finding.title: Replace fixed-millisecond delay polling with emitsInOrder stream matchers in points_balance_dao_test.dart watchBalance tests
finding.why: The two watchBalance tests collect stream emissions into a list via `.listen(emissions.add)` then assert on `emissions.last` after fixed 20ms/50ms sleeps. Under CI contention (parallel shards, a throttled runner) the reactive Drift query stream may not have emitted the post-write value before the sleep expires, producing an intermittent failure on `expect(emissions.last, 50)` that has nothing to do with a real regression — the classic flaky-test pattern that gets 'fixed' by rerunning rather than investigated. profile_dao_test.dart in this same batch (watchProfilesByAccount test) shows the deterministic alternative already in use elsewhere: `expect(stream, emitsInOrder([...]))`, which waits for the actual emission instead of racing a clock.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite both watchBalance tests to assert via `expect(db.pointsBalanceDao.watchBalance(1), emitsInOrder([0, 50, ...]))` (or expectLater) registered before the mutating calls, matching the pattern already used by profile_dao_test.dart's watchProfilesByAccount test, instead of manually collecting emissions behind a fixed sleep.
acceptance_criteria: Both watchBalance tests in points_balance_dao_test.dart use emitsInOrder/expectLater with no fixed-millisecond Future.delayed used purely to wait for a stream emission
Tests pass repeatedly under both default and constrained (--concurrency=1, or CI-like throttled) runs
Rule-0 checker: grep test/**/*_test.dart for `Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds` occurring in the same test body as a preceding `.listen(` call

finding.title: Replace raw DateTime.now() with DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() in DAO test fixture setup
finding.why: TQ-6 requires hermetic tests with no wall-clock reliance. This exact suite's own shared helpers (seedProfile/seedTrack in test/helpers/drift_memory.dart) already route every timestamp through the injectable DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() specifically so the clock can eventually be pinned — but 30 sites across 8 files in this batch bypass it and call DateTime.now() directly for FK-filler timestamp columns. Today the values are unasserted so this is inert, but every raw call site is a future flake waiting to happen the first time a test asserts against 'inserted recently' or a snapshot equality, and none of these 30 sites are routed through any override point.
finding.recommendation: Replace `DateTime.now()` with `DateTimeFactory.nowUtc()` (already available via the existing import chain, or add `import 'package:learning_tracker/core/utils/date_utils.dart';`) or a fixed literal `DateTime.utc(...)` at all 30 sites across the 8 listed files.
acceptance_criteria: All 30 listed DateTime.now() call sites replaced with DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() or a fixed literal
Rule-0 checker: grep test/core/database/daos/**/*.dart for `DateTime.now()`; expect 0 hits

finding.title: Fix misleading 'debitRedemption' test title in points_balance_dao_test.dart that never calls a method by that name

evidence.quote: test('debitRedemption returns false when balance is insufficient', () async {
// Use parentAdjust as a proxy since debitRedemption needs a redemptionId.

finding.why: points_balance_dao.dart has no method named debitRedemption (grep-confirmed against lib/core/database/daos/points_balance_dao.dart: only getBalance/creditCompletion/parentAdjust/createRedemption/fulfilRedemption/declineRedemption exist). The test's own comment admits it substitutes parentAdjust 'as a proxy' — the body actually just re-verifies parentAdjust's clamp-at-zero behavior, already covered 3 tests earlier by 'parentAdjust deducts points (clamped at 0)'. A developer searching for debitRedemption/insufficient-balance coverage will find this test, believe it verifies that path, and waste time chasing a nonexistent API; the real insufficient-balance-on-redemption case is separately and correctly covered by the 'createRedemption returns null when balance is insufficient' test later in the same file.
finding.recommendation: Rename the test to describe what it verifies ('parentAdjust clamps balance at 0 for a large negative delta') or delete it as a duplicate of the adjacent parentAdjust clamp test.
acceptance_criteria: Test renamed to match its actual body, or removed as a duplicate of the parentAdjust clamp test
No reference to a non-existent debitRedemption method remains in the file
